# Rewrite safety fixtures

This directory is the new architecture's fixture root. `acp-contract.json` is a **synthetic, contract-derived** ACP 1 corpus, not captured provider traffic. Its provider profiles are inputs for Pi/Codex/Claude adapter tests; passing the shared corpus alone does not prove provider-specific compatibility. Provider-specific extension and malformed-payload fixtures must be added during typed ACP implementation.

The corpus covers initialize, session creation/prompt, text, thought, tool start/update, plan, usage, permission, elicitation, cancellation, unknown updates and EOF expectations. `test/contract-agent.mjs` is the independent stdio peer used by legacy baselines and the actual new-runtime process contracts. Its `permissions:2`, `permissions:32` and `permissions:33` scenarios support mixed-load and interaction-boundary tests; configuration gates/traces and persistent model fixtures support cancellation and reconciliation failures. Opt-in `WORKBENCH_CONTRACT_NATIVE_STATE` enables `test/helpers/native-fork-fixture.mjs`: a synthetic persistent native-context store with exact hash-checked prefix forks, independent IDs and historical model/mode. Its `streamed-message` scenario emits thought/text deltas sharing an opaque group UUID while recording one complete synthetic native assistant entry; grouped host projection across restart preserves immutable delta payloads. The UUID is not a native entry ID or timestamp. Its inspect output includes Pi-shaped unsafe intermediate points with empty hashes. `WORKBENCH_CONTRACT_FORK_GATE` creates a remote branch before withholding the RPC response, so cancellation/shutdown tests must preserve an uncertain outcome (not pretend remote files were removed). None of this synthetic peer alone establishes real Pi SDK/native-format compatibility. Separately, `pi-sdk-1.3.0-native-offline.json` records sanitized **real Pi CLI/bundled ACP responses on synthetic local history**, captured under isolated HOME/agent configuration with zero model/network requests. Its private capabilities, safe/unsafe tool points and native response decode through a mandatory new Rust DTO test. The explicit `PI_OFFLINE_PI_CLI=/absolute/path/to/pi/dist/cli.js npm run test:native-fork:offline` acceptance also runs the environment-dependent Rust WorkbenchApp case (`--ignored`, never counted as executed by ordinary workspace tests): one-worker native fork, native-load historical settings, removal/restart and immutable receipts, alongside real native image/tool/label/compaction preservation. The real SDK host test additionally matches explicitly synthetic grouped display deltas to a real native assistant prefix (`a1`); it does not record live model streaming. It uses only cached Cargo sources, guards ordinary Node network entrypoints (self-tested, not an OS sandbox), checks marked child exits, and never inherits real account configuration/credentials. Missing SDK/cache is a failed prerequisite, not a passing skip. These provider messages are local/offline, not recordings of live model traffic. The `image-output` / `image-malformed` scenarios exercise immutable agent image staging, metadata-only publication, bad encoding, replacement peer, restart/source removal and corruption checks. Bytes are independent versioned/checksummed payload records; snapshots/events only retain validated image references. MIME signature checks are not a full image decoder. Telegram multipart output now has local HTTP + actual-binary 429/restart, exact archive-byte/topic/order and no-agent-reexecution evidence; PNG/JPEG use photo, GIF animation, WebP document endpoints. This does not establish live Bot acceptance. Image prompt input and tool binary archives remain incomplete. The default new browser now explicitly reads archive images through the typed local extension controller, never URI/path markers; production Chromium smoke decodes the fixture PNG via a data URI and checks no external fetch, along with native fork/form/tool/crash-recovery/cancel flows. Its ACP messages remain synthetic. The production extension/browser and release package now use only the new single host; old daemon/client/browser production entries are removed and a read-only cutover audit checks their absence/import graphs. Explicit local IPC image reads now verify full references and bytes without provider/journal activity, including source removal/restart and a 4 MiB transport/signature fixture. Live user/text/thought/image events expose committed entry IDs and opaque groups without coalescing rows or guessing native timestamps. Only explicit image responses contain base64; snapshots/events stay metadata-only. Parallel topic delivery now has local regressions for eight bounded lanes, blocked media/other-topic progress, uncertain HTTP cancellation/restart, job panic, driver/supervisor abort and a paused ack retaining its join/error/storage lease across cancelled cleanup observers. Actual-binary HTTP fixtures additionally hold an upload response while another topic sends, then verify fatal shutdown closes a held socket and leaves its image intent Pending. This is not SIGKILL process-loss or long-soak acceptance. Outbox admission sequence and deferred-head topic barriers now have restart, 70-record backlog/other-topic progress and actual-binary image-before-later-control-notice evidence. This orders admitted outbox work, not provider timestamps or incomparable domain revisions; old pre-sequence outbox bodies are rejected without migration. Scoped session targets now retain the committed cwd with the immutable image intent (outbox body version 2); history verifies scope identity and rejects workspace mutation, including correctly checksummed mismatched ledgers. Deleted-source delivery tests cover restart, original bytes/topic, no ACP/journal mutation, and denied/unbound/disallowed destinations without image reads. The actual-binary HTTP fixture externally deletes a source during a held upload, fatally shuts down, restarts and delivers the original archived bytes without any ACP trace change. No missing-snapshot load fallback or arbitrary-path/URI authority is introduced; old body/target layouts fail closed without migration. Image URI is deliberately ignored. These image streams are synthetic, not actual model output.

## Three-profile lifecycle and actual host process loss

`app_provider_tests.rs::all_three_synthetic_profiles_cover_plan_usage_permission_forms_cancel_crash_and_native_restart` explicitly runs **each** Pi/Codex/Claude configured profile through profile identity, plan, context/billing usage, invalid/valid permission answers, Unicode/multifield elicitation, waiting-turn cancellation, worker crash/replacement, cold restart and same-native-ID continuation. It uses the shared independent peer (Codex via its separate shell launch), not real provider executables or capability recordings.

`npm run test:workbench:process-loss` runs the actual daemon for all three profiles, archives an image, durably accepts a pending permission turn, and sends **real SIGKILL to the host**. It verifies exact history bytes (no synthetic crash-prefix restoration), immutable prompt receipt replay/no provider reexecution, byte-identical archived image and explicit same-native continuation. Production intentionally refuses the stale socket on restart; only this isolated test validates its dead host's exact socket inode and explicitly removes it before restarting. The fake peer exits on pipe EOF while waiting for permission; this does not establish arbitrary provider/descendant cleanup after host death, automatic production restart, or cgroup isolation. The test environment has isolated HOME and no inherited provider/Bot keys, proxy or NODE_OPTIONS. Cleanup only signals groups proven to belong to this fixture trace.

`npm run test:workbench:soak -- --duration-seconds 600` repeatedly joins the 16-worker/32-interaction/100-query/three-restart mixed regression, the explicit three-provider lifecycle case, and all three real SIGKILL cases. It records phase logs/report under `.test-results/soak-*`, requires at least two full rounds and the requested elapsed duration, fails on any phase failure or absent execution marker, and reports interruption as failure. It is a sustained **local synthetic** workload, not live-provider/Bot traffic or an overnight production soak. It is separate from the short default gate to keep their evidence distinct.

The `tool-metadata` scenario emits v1 tool kind/name, structured diffs/locations, null-preserving patches and explicit empty-list replacements. Mandatory codec tests also cover resource text/links, terminal IDs, unknown/unsupported binary content and opaque raw-input/output round trips at the protocol boundary only. The host runs it under Pi/Codex/Claude synthetic launch profiles and verifies cold restart; actual-binary IPC verifies committed tool events. This is not live provider tool execution. The remaining shared peer scenarios are synthetic, not provider traffic recordings. Do not teach the old peer to accept an invalid new wire format merely to make tests pass.

Existing frozen baseline storage examples are in `../formats/`:

- `history-index.json`: history index example.
- `receipt-completed.json` / `receipt-interrupted.json`: durable operation journal/receipt examples.
- `outbox-event.json`: delivery example.
- `telegram-bridge-state.json`: Telegram state example.
- `preferences-pi.json`: provider settings example.

These samples contain no real user data. They document incompatible legacy formats and must be rejected by the new normal startup paths, not imported implicitly. Old service contract scripts and production readers have been removed; these frozen files remain only as incompatible-format rejection fixtures. Domain reducer, actor mailbox, and persistence tests in the new crate are the new state-transition safety net. All fixtures should remain usable without credentials or a real Bot/model.
